title: 第五章　红色娘子军

en: Five: Red Detachment
zh: 第五章　红色娘子军

en: The story of a rebellious maidservant on Hainan Island who was liberated by a Communist women’s militia became a revolutionary classic in socialist China. At the turn of the millennium, just as her fierce female attitude seemed poised to make a final exit, she leapt—fists clenched and long braid flying—across the surface of a large, four-canvas oil painting by Li Tianpian. Although she held impeccable academy credentials and a teaching position at Beijing’s Central Minorities University, Li struggled to find a way forward. As a young oil painter trained in socialist realism, she found herself wedged between female representational modes of different eras. She had submitted this painting in 1999 as one of two graduation pieces for her Master’s degree from the Hangzhou China Academy of Art. It depicts varied representations of an early Communist women’s detachment formed in the 1930s. Their rebellious posture provides a dramatic contrast with Li’s own delicately rendered appearance within the piece.
zh: 海南岛上一个反抗的女奴被共产党妇女民兵队解放的故事，成为社会主义中国的革命经典。世纪之交，正当她那刚烈的女性姿态似乎准备最后一次退场时，她跃起——双拳紧握，长辫飞扬——横跃在李天翩一幅四联大幅油画的画面上。李天翩拥有无可挑剔的学院资历，并在北京中央民族大学任教，却难以找到前进的道路。作为一名受过社会主义现实主义训练的年轻油画家，她发现自己卡在不同时代的女性再现模式之间。1999年，她把这幅画作为杭州中国美术学院硕士学位的两件毕业作品之一提交。画作描绘了1930年代成立的早期共产党妇女武装的多种再现。她们的叛逆姿态与画中李天翩本人细腻描摹的容貌形成戏剧性对比。

en: (Hongse niangzi jun), a film based on a novel based on actual historical events, was originally released on July 1, 1961, to commemorate the fortieth anniversary of the founding of the Chinese Communist Party. In the decade that followed, the film became a revolutionary ballet and a revolutionary model opera, both of which were then turned back into films.

During the Cultural Revolution, it was one of only eight model plays permitted for public performance. Many in post-Mao China criticize this doctrinaire control of culture, which required performers to enact the same revolutionary plays again and again. Nonetheless these socialist realist dramas were inextricably linked with a twentieth-century Chinese desire to be modern, a desire for social relations that would transcend existing forms. They expressed what Susan Buck-Morss calls the “dreamworld of mass utopia,” a vision shared by those in both the East and West during the Cold War.

While the dream of socialist realism as an emancipatory aesthetic now hung in shreds, this abject form contained a message about the promise and danger of ethnographic detachment and typification, about attempting to convey complex subjectivities through a singular, commanding representation.
zh: 《红色娘子军》改编自小说，小说又取材于真实历史事件，电影于1961年7月1日首映，纪念中国共产党成立四十周年。此后十年间，这部电影被改编为革命芭蕾舞剧和革命样板京剧，两者随后又都被拍成电影。
文化大革命期间，它是获准公开演出的仅有的八部样板戏之一。后毛泽东时代的中国许多人批评这种教条式的文化控制，它要求演员一遍又一遍地搬演同样的革命戏剧。然而，这些社会主义现实主义戏剧与二十世纪中国追求现代性的愿望密不可分，与超越既有形式的社会关系愿望密不可分。它们表达了苏珊·巴克-莫斯（Susan Buck-Morss）所谓“大众乌托邦的梦想世界”，这一愿景在冷战期间东西方都有人共享。
尽管社会主义现实主义作为一种解放美学的梦想如今已成碎片，这一卑微的形式仍包含着关于民族志式抽离与典型化的承诺与危险的信息，关于试图通过单一、统摄性的再现传达复杂主体性的信息。

en: I gleaned my lesson from encounters with this painting and its painter. While Li Tianpian is not particularly well known in China or abroad, her story reveals tensions that many Chinese artists negotiated as the organization of the arts and social life underwent millennial transitions. Occasionally caught up in the excitement of reform-era China’s promise of burgeoning individuality, Li yet remained unwilling to dismiss the propaganda imagery of the Cultural Revolution as national kitsch from a period when time stood still. She provides a lesson in how not to typify or commodify the past, but to reopen its potential and revolutionary promise to extend the range of what it is possible for a woman to do.
zh: 我从与这幅画及其画家的相遇中得到教益。李天翩在中国或国外都不算特别知名，但她的故事揭示了在艺术与社会生活组织经历千禧年转型之际，许多中国艺术家所调停的紧张。李天翩偶尔为改革时期中国对新兴个体性的承诺而振奋，却仍不愿把文化大革命的宣传图像贬为民族媚俗品，视为一个时间停滞时期的产物。她提供了一个教训：如何不把过去典型化或商品化，而是重新打开其潜能和革命承诺，以扩展一个女人可能做什么的范围。

en: Red Souvenir
zh: 红色纪念品

en: When I first met Li Tianpian in 2001 she was thirty-one. She had been teaching in the studio art department of the Central Minorities University for two years.

One of her colleagues, Yuan Yaomin, had arranged for me to attend classes in their department. After spending the morning in a first-year oil painting materials class (a lecture that covered in technical detail various forms of canvas preparation: animal glues, gesso, and tempera), I met Yuan Yaomin and Li Tianpian for lunch. They were the only women in the department and spent much of their free time together. We walked together to a restaurant on campus. A warm spell of mid-April weather had just hit Beijing, and the poplar trees lining the campus walkways had begun to shed fuzzy catkins. The fluff floated through the air like snow and blew into drifts along the sidewalks. We sneezed and laughed as we sat down at our table and picked the downy seeds out of our hair. After lunch, we went back to Yuan Yaomin’s small apartment in the married teachers’ campus dormitory. Her husband worked outside of the university, and her daughter was at school. As we drank tea and chatted, she pulled out some batik wrap-around skirts she’d bought on a recent trip to the south, telling us how cheaply she’d gotten them. We all took turns trying them on. Li Tianpian, who enjoyed dressing up and following the latest fashions, giggled as she strutted back and forth in the tight entryway of the two-room apartment crowded with books, paintings, and furniture. This lighthearted moment distracted from larger worries. During her short experience as a teacher, she began wondering if art really constituted much of a profession anymore. In the current economic climate, she mused, the type of painting she’d been trained in didn’t bring many rewards. She felt stuck in the work-unit existence of a previous era. Before I left that day, she gave me several postcards printed with works she had completed as a graduate student. The largest, most ambitious of the works was a painting titled
(plate 14).
zh: 2001年我第一次见到李天翩时，她三十一岁，已在中央民族大学绘画系任教两年。

她的同事袁耀敏安排我到她们系里听课。上午在一间一年级油画材料课上度过（讲座详细讲解了各种画布制备技术的细节：动物胶、石膏底料和蛋彩），之后我与袁耀敏、李天翩一起吃午饭。她们是系里仅有的两位女性，大部分空闲时间都待在一起。我们一同走到校园里一家餐馆。四月中旬的一股暖流刚刚抵达北京，校园步道两旁的杨树开始飞絮。绒毛像雪一样在空中飘浮，在人行道上被风吹成堆。我们坐下后一边打喷嚏一边笑，从头发里挑出毛茸茸的杨絮。午饭后，我们回到袁耀敏在校园已婚教师宿舍里的小公寓。她丈夫在校外工作，女儿在上学。我们喝茶聊天时，她拿出最近去南方旅行时买的几条蜡染围裹裙，告诉我们买得多便宜。我们轮流试穿。李天翩喜欢打扮、追逐最新时尚，在这套堆满书籍、画作和家具的两居室狭窄门厅里来回走着，咯咯笑着。这个轻松的瞬间暂时掩盖了更大的忧虑。短暂的任教经历让她开始怀疑，艺术是否还算得上一种职业。她说，在当前经济环境下，她受训的那种绘画不会带来多少回报。她觉得自己被困在上一时代的工作单位生存状态中。那天离开前，她送给我几张印有她研究生时期作品的明信片。其中最大、最雄心勃勃的一幅名为《红色纪念品》（图版14）。

en: In the three main canvases of

, each almost two meters tall, the original members of the historic women’s military detachment stand in the background. Their somber, determined faces emerge in slightly blurred gray and black tones. Fragments of historical photographs and a book about the “red women” are layered in a collagelike composition on top of this backdrop. In the immediate foreground, characters from the film and ballet versions of

appear in full color. Painted with more detailed strokes and in greater three-dimensional relief, the ballerina soldier-to-be leaps in the left-hand canvas, frozen in her iconic pose of escape from an evil tyrant. On the opposite side, her enlisted compatriot, dressed in uniform, strikes a confident stance with one hand resting at a belted waist. Li Tianpian appears in a narrower canvas, second from the left, that opens a brief space between contending versions of the historical and the legendary. In this self-portrait, she sits behind an easel with three paintbrushes in her right hand, which also gracefully holds out the outer edge of her skirt. Head cocked to the side, she looks out from behind a large canvas whose back faces the viewer.

She includes herself within the painting in the process of its painting, staring at the viewer in way that creates a triangle between the painter, official representation, and ghostly, layered images of the original women. Like the dramatic performers, she is painted in color, but instead of floating on the surface plane of the painting, she recedes into the perspectival space of the studio classroom where she paints. Warm light floods the background of this personal moment, the peak of her rise through the Chinese art academy system.
zh: 在《红色纪念品》的三块主画布上（每块将近两米高），历史上那支妇女军事武装最初的成员站在背景中。她们阴郁而坚定的面孔以略微模糊的灰色和黑色调浮现。历史照片的片段和一本关于“红色妇女”的书，以拼贴方式叠加在这一背景之上。最前景中，电影和芭蕾舞剧版《红色娘子军》的人物以全彩出现。舞者即将成为战士，用更细致的笔触和更强的三维立体感绘成，在左侧画布上跃起，凝固在她逃离邪恶暴君的经典姿态中。另一侧，她入伍的同伴穿着军装，一手叉腰，摆出自信姿态。李天翩出现在左起第二块较窄的画布上，在历史与传说的相互竞争的版本之间打开一小段空间。在这幅自画像中，她坐在画架后面，右手握着三支画笔，同时优雅地托起裙子的外缘。她侧着头，从一块背对观者的大画布后面望出来。
她把自己画入绘画过程之中，注视观者，在画家、官方再现和历史上真实女兵幽灵般层叠的图像之间构成一个三角形。和那些戏剧演员一样，她以色彩绘成，但她没有漂浮在画面的表面，而是退入她作画的画室课堂的透视空间中。温暖的光线涌入这个个人时刻的背景，那是她在学院体系中升起的高峰。

en: She chose the subject matter for
after a trip during graduate school to Hainan Island, south of Guangdong Province, to

(paint from life). In a later conversation, she talked about what she had hoped to express in the painting. Of her time in Hainan, which in the 1990s developed into a tropical resort destination for urban Chinese tourists, she described ongoing conditions of poverty, as well as local knowledge she gained there about the original female soldiers who became legendary in the later years of Communist artistic repertoire. She spoke quickly in a casual way, punctuating her comments with laughter, even when talking about serious topics.
zh: 她是在研究生期间去广东以南的海南岛写生之后选定《红色纪念品》题材的。后来的一次谈话中，她谈到希望在这幅画中表达什么。谈到在海南的时光——1990年代那里发展成为面向中国城市游客的热带度假胜地——她描述了持续存在的贫困状况，以及她从当地了解到的关于当年真实女兵的知识；这些女兵在后来共产党艺术剧目中成为传奇。她说话很快，语气随意，即使谈到严肃话题，也时常以笑声打断自己的话。

en: The story of the Red Detachment of Women is like this... at the time, they were ordinary people on the island who were oppressed by local landlords and by the Guomindang. The oppression was pretty severe. They lived under cruel conditions.
When I went there, I also found that some people still have very difficult lives. Their houses only have three walls. On the other side, there is no wall.

When I was there, I read some history that I thought was laughable. Back then, when the women joined this female troop, this anti-oppression military detachment, they entered enthusiastically with a kind of revolutionary, romantic zeal. It’s just like a fashion, a trend, I think.

What’s laughable is that after it was all said and done, then a lot of them married some minor officials of the Guomindang. (Laughs.) Now, in reality, if we say they were revolutionaries, then this was a betrayal of their ideals. So afterward, in a later era, when their story was propagandized, this aspect had to be hidden below, it wasn’t talked about. (Laughs.) Just the beginning was told, not the end. Of course, that couldn’t be mentioned.

They had this period of achievement, of the detachment’s resistance. The troop had soldiers, had female commanders, all of them were female soldiers. Then this achievement was changed by the Cultural Revolution into... there was a ballet, as well as an opera... there were films, many artistic forms. Many artistic representations came out. That painting of mine portrays the imagery of these kinds of artistic forms. This is from the ballet... and these are original photographs of them on the road at the revolutionary dawn... and as they were sworn in. (Laughs.) The photographs are from their memorial hall on Hainan Island.

I just wanted to put these artistic representations side by side, and then add historical reality to the picture. To put them all together like this... Think about it, these original women when they started out were so beautiful, wearing military uniforms, with straps and supply bags crisscrossing their chests, wearing these kinds of clothes, some in dresses. They have such a valiant and heroic bearing. Then after they were captured... this picture was taken when they were in jail... they’re wearing old clothes. It wasn’t long after their release that they married the enemy.
zh: 红色娘子军的故事是这样的……当时，她们都是岛上受当地地主和国民党压迫的普通人。压迫相当严重。她们在残酷的条件下生活。
我去的时候，也发现有些人生活仍然非常艰难。他们的房子只有三面墙，另一边没有墙。
我在那里时读了一些历史，觉得很好笑。
当年这些女性加入这支女兵队伍、这支反压迫军事部队时，是满怀一种革命、浪漫的热情进去的。我觉得就像一种时尚、一种潮流。
好笑的是，事情结束之后，她们中很多人嫁给了国民党的小官。（笑。）现在，如果我们说她们是革命者，那这是对她们理想的背叛。所以后来，在另一个时代，当她们的故事被宣传时，这一面必须被藏在下面，不能谈。（笑。）
只讲了开头，没讲结尾。当然，那不能提。
她们有这段成就，这支队伍的抵抗。队伍里有士兵，有女指挥员，全是女兵。后来这一成就被文化大革命改变成了……有芭蕾舞，也有歌剧……有电影，许多艺术形式。许多艺术再现都出来了。我那张画描绘的就是这些艺术形式的形象。这是芭蕾舞的……这些是她们在革命黎明行军时的原始照片……以及她们宣誓时的照片。（笑。）照片来自海南岛的纪念馆。
我只想把这些艺术再现并置，然后给画面加入历史现实。就这样把它们全部放在一起……
想想看，历史上这些真实的女性刚开始时多么美丽，穿着军装，带子和补给袋交叉绑在胸前，穿着这样的衣服，有些人穿裙子。她们有那样英勇豪迈的姿态。后来她们被捕……这张照片是她们在狱中拍的……她们穿着旧衣服。获释没多久，她们就嫁给了敌人。

en: She wasn’t happy with the final result of her painting and said she wanted to paint it over again.
zh: 她并不满意这幅画的最终效果，说想重画一遍。

en: I think that when I painted it, my technique was limited, my visual range was relatively shallow, so I wasn’t able to effectively express my idea... I wasn’t able to find a more suitable means of expression. My application of color was no good. I think it should be brighter and clearer, the red accents and everything... the imagery could have been painted in a more individualistic style, with more painterly flavor, with more painterly feeling. Some places are too realistic, and then speaking of realism, other places are not realistic enough, so I’m still not very satisfied, even after completing this big painting.
zh: 我觉得我画的时候技术有限，视野比较窄，所以没能有效表达我的想法……我没能找到更合适的表达方式。我的色彩运用不好。我觉得应该更明亮、更清晰，红色的强调之类……形象本可以画得更有个人风格，更有绘画气息，更有绘画感觉。有些地方太写实，说到写实，另一些地方又不够写实，所以即使画完这幅大画，我仍然不太满意。

en: Shuang nü ti
zh: 双女体

en: Li Tianpian explained that she chose to major in oil painting as an undergraduate at the art academy because of the technical difficulty. And the colors attracted her. Chinese ink painting seemed too loose and easy compared with the rigor, objectivity, and precision required for realistic oil painting.
zh: 李天翩解释说，她在本科时选择油画专业，是因为技术难度，也因为色彩吸引她。与写实油画所要求的严谨、客观和精确相比，中国水墨画似乎过于松散、容易。

en: She said Soviet-style academic realism had exerted a strong influence on Chinese oil painting over the last century. Painters who studied abroad in the Soviet Union brought this style, as well as dominant subject matter and compositional conventions, back to China.

She told me that the brushstrokes of this style differed from European classicism, that they were broader and blunter, more suited to propaganda needs of bold, straightforward communication. Many of her high school and university teachers subscribed to the Soviet School of painting and followed its teaching methodology.
zh: 她说，苏联式学院写实主义在过去一个世纪对中国油画产生了强烈影响。留学苏联的画家把这种风格，以及主导的题材和构图惯例带回中国。
她告诉我，这种风格的笔触不同于欧洲古典主义，更宽、更钝，更适合大胆、直截了当的宣传需要。她高中和大学的许多老师都属于苏联画派，遵循其教学方法。

en: When I first glanced over the spring 2001 semester course schedule for the oil painting department at the Central Minorities University, where Li Tianpian and Yuan Yaomin taught, none of the offerings struck me as that different from the studio art classes I had attended as an undergraduate in the United States: materials, oil painting, sketching, figure drawing, and painting. The only surprise was that male and female figure work were divided into separate sections, as if emphasizing specialized skills needed to render anatomical difference, and the female figure section was further subdivided into “single female figure” and “double female figure” (

). When I expressed curiosity about these categories, Li and Yuan didn’t understand why I found them so unusual. They explained that painting two figures together added another level of difficulty. When I pushed them on why “double female figure” did not have a “double male figure” equivalent on the teaching schedule, they laughed, saying they’d never thought about this question before. The only explanation they could come up with was that people preferred to look at female nudes; they were more beautiful.
zh: 我第一次查看李天翩和袁耀敏任教的中央民族大学油画系2001年春季课程表时，没觉得哪门课与我在美国读本科时上的绘画课有明显不同：材料、油画、素描、人体素描和绘画。唯一令人惊讶的是男女体写生被分成不同单元，仿佛是在强调描绘解剖差异所需的专门技能，而女体单元又进一步细分为“单人女体”和“双女体”（shuang nü ti）。我表达好奇时，李天翩和袁耀敏不明白我为什么觉得这很不寻常。她们解释说，把两个人体画在一起会增加一层难度。当我追问为什么课表上没有与“双女体”相对应的“双男体”时，她们笑了，说以前从未想过这个问题。她们能想到的唯一解释是，人们更喜欢看女性裸体；她们更美。

en: Several of the paintings Li Tianpian completed in her final year as a graduate student depict two female nudes, lying or sitting together. When I later asked her more about the rationale behind studio studies of this shuang nü ti type, she described a pedagogical method of challenging students with increasing levels of difficulty. The human figure already represents an advance beyond still life studies. Only upper level students can paint the nude figure. In the beginning, students first work at mastering the human head, often from plaster casts. Students then advance to head and torso studies, usually working from a clothed model, and then to the full figure. During their third year, they can finally sketch and paint nudes. They begin with single figures, and eventually teachers present them with studio poses involving two nude models together. Li Tianpian explained to me that the subtlety required for accurate depiction of the human form is doubled with two figures contained within a single frame. Students must also learn to deal with the tonal, spatial, and compositional relationship between the two figures: “Everything becomes more complex.” She believed that this teaching method of progressively heightened levels of technical difficulty came from the Soviet Union, as did the convention of double figure exercises. She remembered seeing some “double male figure” studies in Chinese reproductions of Soviet textbooks, and while she had also painted some of these over the course of her studies, the shuang nü ti remained the favored form.
zh: 李天翩研究生最后一年完成的几幅画描绘了两个一起躺着或坐着的女性裸体。后来我向她进一步询问课堂上这类“双女体”练习的理论依据时，她描述了用递增难度挑战学生的教学方法。人体习作已比静物习作进了一阶。只有高年级学生才能画裸体。一开始，学生先掌握头部的描绘，常以石膏像为对象，然后进阶到头部和躯干，通常使用着衣模特，再进阶到全身。到第三年，他们终于可以速写和描绘裸体。他们从单个人体开始，最终老师会布置两个裸体模特一起的课堂姿势。李天翩向我解释，在一个画面中容纳两个人体，准确描绘人体形态所需的细腻功夫便加倍。学生还必须学会处理两个人体之间的色调、空间和构图关系：“一切都变得更复杂。”她认为这种逐步提高技术难度的教学方法来自苏联，双人体练习的惯例也来自苏联。她记得在中国翻印的苏联教科书中见过一些“双男体”习作，虽然她在求学期间也画过一些，但“双女体”仍是最受青睐的形式。

en: This classroom exercise emphasized technical proficiency over individual modes of expression. The female bodies represented academic mastery of anatomical correctness, coloration, space, and composition. Shuang nü ti showed up in the work of several other painters I interviewed. Even for those who after graduation explored styles of painting other than realism, double female figures remained an occasional part of their vocabulary. When I asked one of these painters about her painting of two women lying together on a bed—a bold expressionist composition with bright colors and thick, loose brushstrokes—she anticipated the motivation behind my question. “Foreigners often think this series is of lesbians,” she laughed. “That’s what they see. To me, they are just shuang nü ti.”
zh: 这种课堂练习强调技术熟练而非个人表达方式。女性身体代表对解剖正确性、色彩、空间和构图的学院掌握。“双女体”也出现在我采访的其他几位画家作品中。即使那些毕业后探索写实之外绘画风格的人，双女体仍然是她们偶尔使用的语汇。当我问其中一位画家关于她画两个女人一起躺在床上的作品——一幅色彩明亮、笔触粗放的大胆表现主义构图——她预料到我问题背后的动机。“外国人常觉得这个系列是女同性恋，”她笑着说，“他们看到的就是这个。对我来说，它们只是‘双女体’。”

en: FIG 5.01 Li Tianpian,
, 1998. Oil on canvas, 146 cm × 114 cm.

children: 图5.01　李天翩，《古典美》，1998年。布面油画，146厘米×114厘米。

en: Li Tianpian’s
(figure 5.01), a shuang nü ti painted one year before she completed

, depicts two women lying diagonally across bunched swaths of cloth on the floor. One woman, fully nude, lies on her side, with her back to the second women, clad in black bra, underwear, and stockings, who lies on her stomach. Both women have their eyes closed. Both wear watches (the models have shed their clothes, but not the time pieces that will allow them to gauge how much longer they must hold the pose; both have their arms positioned so they may easily glance at their watches). At the top of the painting, two potted ferns, placed close enough for their leaves to touch, echo the relationship of the two models. When I asked Li Tianpian about the subject matter in this painting, she mentioned only how difficult the folds in the draperies had been to render.
zh: 李天翩的《古典美》（图5.01）是一幅“双女体”，作于她完成《红色纪念品》前一年，描绘两个女人斜躺在地板上堆叠的布幅上。一名女子全裸侧卧，背对第二名女子；后者俯卧，穿着黑色胸罩、内裤和丝袜。两个女人都闭着眼睛，都戴着手表（模特脱去了衣服，却没有脱去计时器，以便知道还要保持这个姿势多久；她们的手臂都摆成可以轻易瞥见手表的位置）。画面上方，两盆蕨类植物靠得很近，叶子相触，呼应两位模特的关系。当我向李天翩询问这幅画的题材时，她只提到布褶有多难画。

en: She continued, “As a graduate student, I wanted to depart from extremely classical or traditional styles, because they have no individuality, but I don’t think I’ve succeeded.” She laughed, and then became momentarily serious and introspective. “I continually think about this problem. This issue of mine, the challenge of painting, it’s a lifelong thing, I think...”
zh: 她接着说：“读研究生时，我想摆脱极其古典或传统的风格，因为它们没有个性，但我觉得自己没成功。”她笑了，随后短暂地严肃起来，陷入内省。“我不断思考这个问题。我的这个问题，绘画的挑战，我想是一辈子的事……”

en: “There’s still time,” I said, and we both laughed.
zh: “还有时间，”我说，我们都笑了。

, directed by Xie Jin, 1961. Introductory text and credits appear superimposed over this woodcut print.

children: 图5.02　谢晋导演《红色娘子军》片头字幕美术，1961年。片头文字与演职员表叠加在这幅木刻版画上。

en: Enmity
zh: 仇恨

en: The opening image of the Shanghai film production of
is a graphically striking woodcut print in tones of red, black, and gray (figure 5.02).

It depicts women in army uniform on the battlefield. They wear caps with red stars and carry red flags, pitchforks, rifles, and sickles in silhouette against a pale red sky. In a triangular composition reminiscent of Delacroix’s
, a single woman rises higher than the rest on the horizon with one arm raised.

The following text, accompanied by a dramatic voice-over rendition of it, then appears on top of this image: “This battle story of a heroic daughter took place on Hainan Island in the south of the Motherland in 1930. That was an era of extreme suffering for Chinese people, as well as the era in which the Red Army of young workers and peasants was established.”
zh: 上海电影制片厂《红色娘子军》的开场画面，是一幅红、黑、灰三色的木刻版画，视觉冲击力强烈（图5.02）。
它描绘战场上的女兵。她们戴着缀红星的帽子，扛着红旗、拿着叉、步枪和镰刀，身影映衬在淡红色天空下。在一种让人想起德拉克洛瓦《自由引导人民》的三角形构图中，一名女子高举一臂，在众人之上耸立天际。
随后，这段文字伴随戏剧性的画外朗诵出现在画面上：“这是英雄女儿的战斗故事，发生在祖国南方的海南岛上，时间是1930年。那是中国人民苦难深重的年代，也是年轻的工农红军创立的年代。”

en: At the beginning of the film, the heroine Wu Qionghua runs away from a household in Guomindang-controlled Coconut Village, where she serves as a slave girl. The henchmen of the tyrannical landlord Nan Batian quickly capture her. They chain her wrists to the ceiling in a basement prison and whip her, until the sympathetic eyes of a Communist spy, the dashing Hong Changqing disguised as a wealthy Overseas Chinese merchant, fall on her tortured body. He tells Nan Batian that he needs a servant and convinces the landlord to give him the troublesome Qionghua. After leaving the estate, he frees Qionghua, gives her some money for the road, and directs her toward Red Stone County, where she’s heard a revolutionary women’s detachment is stationed. On the way, she meets Honglian, another woman equally determined to join the detachment, and together they arrive in Red Stone Country, where the female troops perform a military review for a group of high-ranking male officials assembled on a stage above the field. As the troops file off screen, Qionghua and Honglian break through the barricade and run after them. In the next scene, a female soldier introduces them to the commanding officer of her troop.
zh: 影片开头，女主角吴琼花从国民党控制的椰林寨一户人家逃出，在那里她充当婢女。恶霸地主南霸天的爪牙很快抓住她。他们把她手腕吊在地下室牢房的天花板上鞭打，直到一名共产党侦察员同情的目光落在这具受刑的身体上——他衣着潇洒，伪装成富有的南洋华侨商人洪常青。他告诉南霸天自己需要一个仆人，说服地主把麻烦的琼花交给他。离开庄园后，他释放琼花，给她一些盘缠，指引她去红石县——她听说那里驻扎着一支革命妇女武装。路上，她遇到另一个同样决心参军的女子红莲；她们一起来到红石县。女兵们正在一片场地上接受检阅，一群男性高级官员聚集在场地高处的台上。队伍列队离开画面时，琼花和红莲冲破阻拦，追了上去。下一场中，一名女兵把她们介绍给队伍的指挥员。

en: Soldier Reporting that two commoners have arrived.
Commander (Walks over to Qionghua and Honglian) What are you doing here?
Qionghua We’ve come to be woman soldiers.
Commander Right, when we were reviewing the troops, you came in. That was very daring.
Qionghua Daring, yes, I can do anything.
Commander Proletariat class?
Qionghua (Looks around) What?
Soldier Do you have any status?
Qionghua I am a slave girl. I don’t have anything.
Commander Good, you’re fine. (Looks at Honglian) And you?
Honglian I also don’t know if I have any status. I was sold to someone when I was ten years old.
Commander Of course that’s proletariat, fine.
Soldiers (Giggling to each other) What a pity to have them... do you think their marriages have already been arranged... really!
Commander (Shushing them) Quiet down! Really! (To Qionghua and Honglian) You two go take care of formalities.
Qionghua Aren’t you the commander?
Commander Yes.
Qionghua Then if you say we’re in, we’re in.
Commander (Quiets down the laughing soldiers again) A little more order! You need to go apply and say why you want to join.

Qionghua Why I want to join... (marches over to the commander)... you have to ask why! (She rips open the collar of her blouse to show the lash marks on her chest.) For this! To protest! To get revenge! To kill those tyrants! Cannibals! Skin them alive! I... I... (She stops speaking and covers her chest back up as the uniformed male leader Hong Changqing, no longer in his merchant disguise, walks into the scene.)
zh: 士兵　报告，来了两个老百姓。
连长（走向琼花和红莲）你们来干什么？
琼花　我们来当女兵。
连长　对，我们检阅的时候，你们闯进来了。胆子不小啊。
琼花　胆子大，我什么都敢。
连长　是无产阶级吗？
琼花（环顾）什么？
士兵　有身价吗？
琼花　我是奴隶，什么都没有。
连长　好，行。（看红莲）你呢？
红莲　我也不知道自己有没有身价。我十岁时被卖给了别人。
连长　那当然是无产阶级，行。
女兵们（相互笑）可惜她们……你们说她们的婚事是不是已经定了……真的！
连长（嘘她们）安静！真是的！（对琼花和红莲）你们两个去办手续。
琼花　你不是连长吗？
连长　是。
琼花　那你说我们行，我们就行。
连长（再次让笑的女兵安静）有点秩序！你们需要去申请，说明为什么要参加。
琼花　为什么要参加……（走到连长面前）……你还要问为什么！（她撕开上衣领口，露出胸前的鞭痕。）为了这个！要控诉！要报仇！要杀那些暴君！吃人的东西！剥他们的皮！我……我……（她停住，掩上胸口，穿军装的男领导洪常青——已不再是商人伪装——走进画面。）

en: In response to the female commander’s instructions to apply for entry by explaining why she wants to join the Communist army, Qionghua exposes her wounds (figure 5.03). An audible ripping accompanies the visual image. In this classic cinematic take on a revolutionary moment of “speaking bitterness,” the woman’s body bears the marks of patriarchal feudal oppression. Her politics of exposure become pedagogical; they move the viewer to sympathy but also demonstrate Qionghua’s need for political training. Under the tutelage of party leaders in the military, particularly the handsome male officer Hong Changqing, Qionghua learns through error to transform personal rage against her former master into class solidarity. After being shown a map of China and realizing that she is part of a larger, collective struggle, she devotes herself to the party. Shortly before Changqing dies a martyr to the cause, he informs Qionghua that her application to the party has been accepted. After his death, she carries his accouterments of authority—document case and pocket watch—and takes up his role as party representative.
zh: 面对女指挥员让她说明为什么参军、以便提出申请的要求，琼花露出伤口（图5.03）。视觉图像伴有听得见的撕裂声。在这个经典的电影化“诉苦”革命时刻，女人的身体带着父权封建压迫的印记。她的暴露政治具有教育意义：既感动观者同情，也表明琼花需要政治训练。在部队里党的领导人，尤其是英俊的男军官洪常青的教诲下，琼花从错误中学习，把对旧主人的个人愤怒转化为阶级团结。在看到一幅中国地图、意识到自己是一场更大集体斗争的一部分后，她献身于党。常青为事业牺牲前不久，告诉琼花她的入党申请已被接受。他死后，她接过他象征权威的随身物件——公文包和怀表——承担起党代表的角色。

en: Film scholar Shuqin Cui describes Hong Changqing as a heroic, transcendent figure who “exemplifies not an individual identity but rather the sociopolitical and cinematic criteria for art production.”

Socialist realism, a variant of modernist realism, attempted to document the experience of a collectivity, a class of people, rather than that of an individual. In its utopian ambitions, to create through cultural production a society that did not yet exist, this revolutionary class does not recognize itself as such. That was the goal of artistic creation, to generate this sense of identification and fold it into political ideology. The male communist Chang-qing serves as this figure for Qionghua (and viewers of the film), until she eventually learns to speak through his voice and, clothed in the gender-neutral uniform of the party, transcendently replaces him. In Cui’s analysis, “Because of her dual identities as social victim and political alien, the repressed female subaltern is a signifying subject unable to speak up for herself, yet she embodies sociocultural meanings. As the sublime and the subaltern enter into a gendered relation, sexual difference is reduced to rhetorical indoctrination, for the task of the sublime is to teach the subaltern how to speak.”
zh: 电影学者崔淑琴把洪常青描述为一个英雄、超凡的人物，他“所体现的不是个人身份，而是艺术生产的社会政治与电影标准”。

社会主义现实主义是现代主义现实主义的一个变体，试图记录一个集体、一个阶级的经验，而非个人的经验。在其乌托邦雄心——通过文化生产创造一个尚不存在的社会——中，这个革命阶级尚未认出自身。艺术创作的目标就是产生这种认同感，并将其纳入政治意识形态。男性共产党人常青充当琼花（以及电影观众）的这一形象，直到她最终学会通过他的声音说话，穿上党的性别中立制服，超凡地取代他。按崔淑琴的分析：“由于她具有社会受害者和政治异类的双重身份，受压抑的底层女性是一个无法为自己发声的表意主体，却又承载社会文化意义。当崇高者与底层者进入一种性别化关系时，性别差异被化约为修辞灌输，因为崇高者的任务就是教导底层者如何说话。”

en: FIG 5.03 Qionghua exposes her wounds,
, directed by Xie Jin, 1961.

children: 图5.03　琼花露出伤口，谢晋导演《红色娘子军》，1961年。

en: With each new technological development, of perspectival painting, photography, and cinema, proponents of realism have lauded their fidelity to life and facility at recording the real. (The same might be said about ethnographic data collection methods.) Postmodern theorists have, in turn, shown the lie of realism: how authoritative modes of representation interpret, persuade, and discipline. The theory of Soviet Realism adopted in China through the arts did not purport to represent the real, but rather to create the “typical” for heightened political effect. The premier issue of

(Fine arts), an official art journal founded in January 1954, published the first of many monthly translations of essays on Soviet art theory. “On the Problem of the Typical in Painting” defines the “typical” as “not only the frequently seen things but those with substance which most completely and most keenly express a certain social power.” The author continues, “According to Marxist-Leninism, the typical is not a sort of statistical average. The typical is the same as the substance of a certain socio-historical phenomenon; it is not simply the most common, frequently occurring, and ordinary phenomenon. Intentional exaggeration or emphasis on a phenomenon does not exclude the typical; it is a more complete exploration of it.... The question of the typical is under all circumstances a political question.”

While the oppression of subaltern women on Hainan might have been “a sort of statistical average,” embodying sociocultural meaning and revolutionary potential, they gain voice only through the typification of Qionghua’s political transformation in the likeness of Changqing—an act of ventriloquism combined with a costume change.
zh: 随着透视绘画、摄影和电影等每一种新技术的发展，现实主义的拥护者都称赞其对生活的忠实以及记录现实的能力。（对民族志数据收集方法也可以这样说。）后现代理论家则反过来揭示了现实主义的谎言：权威的再现方式如何解释、说服和规训。通过艺术传入中国的苏联现实主义理论并不声称再现现实，而是为了加强政治效果创造“典型”。1954年1月创刊的官方艺术杂志《美术》第一期，发表了此后每月连载的苏联艺术理论文章译文的第一篇。《论绘画中的典型问题》把“典型”定义为“不仅时常看见的事物，而且是那些最充分、最敏锐地表现某种社会力量、具有本质性的事物”。作者接着说：“根据马克思列宁主义，典型不是一种统计平均值。典型等同于某一社会历史现象的本质；它不只是最常见、最频繁发生、最普通的现象。有意夸大或强调某一现象并不排除典型；这是对典型更完整的探索……典型问题在任何情况下都是政治问题。”
海南底层女性所受的压迫或许是“一种统计平均值”，承载社会文化意义和革命潜能，她们却只有通过琼花以常青形象完成的政治转变的典型化才获得声音——这是一种腹语术，加上换装。

en: At the film’s end, Qionghua glances down at her inherited pocket watch, and the Red Detachment of Women march into the future. They sing: “March on and march on. We shoulder serious responsibilities as soldiers and embody deep enmity as women. In the past, Hua Mulan joined the army in the name of her father; today women of the detachment fight for the people.” In the same line that celebrates women marching in the same uniform as men, gender difference is also reinscribed. Soldiers, joined by class grievance, shoulder serious responsibilities; women, vessel-like, embody deep enmity. Cross-dressing, in the generic mode of Hua Mulan from the mythic Chinese past, is not liberatory in a personal sense but a socially acceptable and even publicly mandated form of gender transgression for the greater social good, whether that be family or nation. The body of the woman beneath the soldier’s uniform (a dialectical tension between official discourses about
distinction and “men and women are the same”) inspires the revolutionary imperative of revenge, blood debts that must be paid in kind.
knowingly concealed, a relinquishment rather than expression of individual subjectivity, becomes a cultural symbol of establishing a new moral order. Yet at the same time, in this transgression
extends the range of what is possible, even thinkable, for women to aspire to, as revolutionaries, painters, and authors of their own image.
zh: 影片结尾，琼花低头看了一眼继承来的怀表，红色娘子军向未来行进。她们唱道：“向前进，向前进。战士的责任重，妇女的冤仇深。古有花木兰替父去从军，今有娘子军扛枪为人民。”在同一句歌词赞美女性与男性穿同样制服行进的同时，性别差异也被重新铭刻。战士因阶级仇恨而联合，肩负重任；女人则像容器一样，承载深仇大恨。按照中国神话过去花木兰的类型模式，女扮男装并非个人意义上的解放，而是为了更大的社会利益——家庭或国家——被社会接受、甚至公开要求的性别越界形式。军装下的女人身体（关于男女有别和“男女都一样”的官方话语之间的辩证张力）激发革命的复仇命令，血债必须血偿。她有意隐藏身体，不是表达而是放弃个人主体性，成为建立新道德秩序的文化象征。然而与此同时，在这种越界中，她扩展了女性作为革命者、画家和自己形象作者可以追求、甚至想象的范围。

en: Li Tianpian, as she sits in the drag of a new era, delicately holding out the edge of her skirt, admires these discarded women in a way that jostles contemporary presumptions about what is “naturally” feminine or masculine: “Think about it, these original women when they started out were so beautiful, wearing military uniforms, with straps and supply bags crisscrossing their chests...” The Red Detachment does not represent a fixed point in time, but a shifting point of reference to critique the 1990s Chinese notion of men and women as essences that can’t be changed but only played with, bought and sold on a market that demands sexed bodies to fulfill commodified forms of desire.
zh: 李天翩坐在新时代的装扮中，优雅地托起裙边，以搅动当代关于何为“天然”女性或男性的预设的方式仰慕这些被丢弃的女人：“想想看，历史上这些真实的女性刚开始时多么美丽，穿着军装，带子和补给袋交叉绑在胸前……”《红色娘子军》不代表时间中的固定点，而是一个移动的参照点，用来批判1990年代中国关于男女本质不可改变、只能被玩弄、在市场买卖的观念——市场要求有性别的身体来满足商品化的欲望形式。

en: For the painter, a different order of difficulty arises at the point of learning to translate “life drawing or painting” studies (in which nudes represent the height of technical difficulty) into the “typical” of socialist or reform-era political imagery. The models in Li Tianpian’s

painting have been stripped of soldier uniform and appear nearly nude in another manifestation of “liberatory,” titillating feminine drag: sheer black stockings, panties, and brassiere. But this image also contains a punctum, a mundane detail that unravels its bland fantasy. The wristwatches worn by the models appear as an accident of the painter’s careful attention to the detail of what exists before her eye in the studio; they signal the tedium of the present, as the models wait for their next break and their bodies grow stiff in the pose they must hold for the painter to capture. They remind us that they have been hired to lie still, but that time does not stand still. Instead it warps in a disconcerting way, past folding into future, amplifying sacrifice, failure, reversal. The pocket watch inherited by Wu Qionghua from Hong Changqing in the filmic version of

signaled the time for coordinated military advance, toward a teleologically determined future. The wounds lashed into the woman’s flesh were covered up by a soldier’s uniform, to create a valiant bearing that made her beautiful in a typological way. Now the whitening creams of reform-era feminine beauty, or oil pigments of titanium white mixed with yellow ochre and a hint of cadmium red, smooth the wrinkles from flesh laid bare again.
zh: 对画家而言，另一层面的困难出现在学习把“人体写生”习作（其中裸体代表技术难度的顶峰）转化为社会主义或改革时期政治图像的“典型”时。李天翩《古典美》中的模特被剥去士兵制服，几乎全裸，呈现另一种“解放的”、撩人的女性装扮：透明黑丝袜、内裤和胸罩。但这幅图像也包含一个刺点，一个使平淡幻想解体的平凡细节。模特佩戴的手表显得像是画家对画室眼前存在之物细致关注的偶然产物；它们标示出当下的沉闷，模特等待下一次休息，身体在必须保持供画家捕捉的姿势中变得僵硬。它们提醒我们，她们是被雇来静止躺着的，但时间并未静止。相反，它以令人不安的方式扭曲，过去折叠进未来，放大牺牲、失败、反转。电影版《红色娘子军》中，吴琼花从洪常青那里继承的怀表，标示协同军事推进、迈向目的论所决定未来的时间。抽打在女人肉体上的伤口被军装遮盖，制造出英勇姿态，使她在类型意义上美丽。如今，改革时期女性美的美白霜，或钛白与土黄、少许镉红混合的油画颜料，抚平了再次裸露肉体上的皱纹。

en: Revolutionary Theater
zh: 革命剧场

en: In the early 1960s, Mao Zedong’s wife Jiang Qing began her campaign to revolutionize the performing arts of opera, music, dance, and film. She reached the height of her influence during the Cultural Revolution by turning her attention to a realm from which she had once tried to distance herself. In 1930s Shanghai she had worked as a rising stage and screen actress at the same time as her involvement in the Communist underground as a cultural worker. In later years, critics questioned her early commitment to the party by pointing to the fame she had sought as a film star; she claimed in response that capitalistic film companies had forced her to sign exploitative contracts with them.

Her personal history also included bitter memories of her father’s abuse of her mother, which led her mother to flee with her as a child into the position of servant in a number of households. As Jiang dedicated herself to a theater of revolutionary heroism, she explained that her focus on the arts emerged from a belief that the superstructure had fallen out of step with the economic base: it lagged behind, creating a social vulnerability that made a “capitalist restoration” possible. Jiang aimed to push the superstructure ahead, advocating ongoing class struggle through a transformation of cultural forms. This tenet of her political theorizing, adapted from Mao, that the superstructure could lead the base, reversed the usual temporality forced by orthodox analysts on these metaphorical concepts in Marx’s writings. In the abstraction of base and superstructure into separate, observable segments of human activity, they were most often described as sequential, “first material production, then consciousness, then politics and culture.”

The avant-gardism of Jiang’s activism did not attempt to dissolve the boundaries between art and the everyday, as did contemporary Western theories of the avant-garde, but to propel culture to the forefront of a bid to make China the center of world revolutionary socialism.
zh: 1960年代初，毛泽东的妻子江青开始推动戏曲、音乐、舞蹈和电影等表演艺术的革命。文化大革命期间，她把注意力转向一个曾试图与之保持距离的领域，影响力达到顶峰。1930年代的上海，她一边作为崭露头角的舞台和银幕演员工作，一边作为文化工作者参与共产党地下活动。后来，批评者以她追求电影明星名声为由，质疑她早期对党的忠诚；她回应说，资本主义电影公司强迫她签订了剥削性合同。

她的个人经历还包括父亲虐待母亲的痛苦记忆，母亲因此带着年幼的她逃离，到好几户人家当仆人。江青投身革命英雄主义剧场时解释说，她对艺术的关注源于一种信念：上层建筑已经落后于经济基础，造成社会脆弱性，使“资本主义复辟”成为可能。江青旨在推动上层建筑前进，倡导通过文化形式的转变继续阶级斗争。这一政治理论信条改编自毛泽东，即上层建筑可以先于经济基础发展，颠倒了正统分析者强加于马克思著作中这些隐喻概念的通常时间顺序。在把基础和上层建筑抽象为可观察的独立人类活动领域时，它们最常被描述为先后相继：“首先是物质生产，然后是意识，然后是政治和文化。”
江青行动主义的先锋主义不像当代西方先锋理论那样试图消解艺术与日常生活的边界，而是把文化推到争取让中国成为世界革命社会主义中心的前沿。

en: In 1963, she began her preparations for a revolutionary model ballet based on the story of the famous Hainan Island Communist Women’s Detachment. When she first spoke to the dancers at the Beijing Dance Institute, she told them that the 1961 film had been flawed but she believed in her ability to mold the narrative to express true revolutionary principles. The stage production would eventually be lauded as a realization of Mao’s concept to “make the old serve the new and things foreign serve things Chinese.” Jiang Qing’s English-language biographer Roxanne Witke claims that this and her other model dramas also created a theater based on the theme of revenge, an emotional substratum largely ignored in doctrinaire Marxist-Leninist political theory.

Mao, in his “Talks at the Yan’an Conference on Literature and Art,” had called for cultural workers to provoke love for the peasantry and hatred for their enemies—tyrannical landlords, Guomindang rulers, and Japanese imperialists. Jiang’s theater purified vengeance, directing how and against whom it could be unleashed, replacing the terror of history’s uncertainty with the inevitability of bright and shining heroics for the masses to emulate.
zh: 1963年，她开始准备一部以海南岛著名共产党妇女武装故事为基础的革命芭蕾舞剧。她第一次对北京舞蹈学院的舞者讲话时说，1961年的电影有缺陷，但她相信自己有能力改造叙事，表达真正的革命原则。这部舞台作品最终被誉为毛泽东“古为今用，洋为中用”理念的实现。江青的英文传记作者罗克珊·维特克（Roxanne Witke）声称，这部和其他样板戏也创造了一种以复仇为主题的剧场，这种情感基底在教条主义的马克思列宁主义政治理论中大多被忽视。
毛泽东在《在延安文艺座谈会上的讲话》中曾号召文化工作者激发对农民的爱和对敌人的恨——恶霸地主、国民党统治者和日本帝国主义者。江青的剧场提纯了复仇，规定如何、向谁发泄，用群众应当效仿的光辉英雄的必然性，取代历史不确定性的恐怖。

en: In the ballet version of

, the heroine Qionghua (“Jade Flower”) becomes Qinghua (“Clear China”). She flees on her own from the tyrant’s dungeon, but his guards chase her down and whip and beat her viciously. They leave her for dead. A violent rainstorm wakes Qinghua from her stupor. She rises to dance before fainting again. The Red Army officer Hong Changqing finds her and points her on the road to revolution. When she arrives at the Red Army base, she runs forward to press her face to the flag. The members of the detachment are identified as women of the Li ethnic nationality, to further accentuate the oppression of old China against minorities. The soldiers welcome Qinghua, and she pours out her story of suffering in a dance that reenacts how she was almost beaten to death. She joins the unit and learns with the others sitting before a blackboard on which the following lesson has been written: “Only by emancipating all mankind can the proletariat achieve its own final emancipation.” They overthrow the tyrant, liberate the people of Coconut Grove, and after Hong Changqing dies a defiant martyr to the cause, Qinghua declares: “Oh, Party, you rescued me from an abyss of bitterness. You raised me to maturity in the flames of class struggle. I pledge to model myself after Comrade Hong. I shall be a revolutionary and never leave the battlefield until the red flag waves over the Five Continents and Four Seas!”
zh: 在芭蕾版《红色娘子军》中，女主角吴琼花（“玉花”）变成清华（“清朗的中国”）。她独自逃出暴君的地牢，却遭到他的卫兵追捕，被残酷鞭打。他们把她丢下等死。一场猛烈的暴雨使清华从昏迷中醒来。她起身舞蹈，又昏了过去。红军军官洪常青发现她，指引她走上革命道路。她到达红军根据地时，跑上前把脸贴在红旗上。娘子军成员被设定为黎族妇女，以进一步强调旧中国对少数民族的压迫。战士们欢迎清华，她在一段再现自己如何几乎被打死的舞蹈中倾诉苦难经历。她加入部队，和其他人一起坐在写有如下教导的黑板前学习：“无产阶级只有解放全人类，才能最后解放自己。”她们推翻暴君，解放椰林寨人民；洪常青为事业英勇牺牲后，清华宣誓：“党呵，是您把我从苦海里救出来，是您在阶级斗争的风雨中把我培育成长。我立志做洪常青那样的革命者，永远跟着党，永远干革命，直到红旗插遍五洲四海！”

en: The choreography drew elements from classical ballet as it had been introduced to China in the 1950s by Russian ballet instructors and from Chinese opera. This synthesis of movements drawn from two bourgeois repertoires was used to advocate proletariat heroes. In particular, female dancers made a sharp break from the fragile, feminine movements of the past, and the poor, working classes were represented as strong and positive rather than vulgar. Jiang Qing attended to details as fine as the art of patching. Worn work clothes of proletarian characters could not appear plain or shabby through “plain realism” or sloppy patches. Jiang directed the company tailors to craft beautiful costumes that represented hardship artistically. In
(figure 5.04), long black whip lashes are painted across the legs, arms, chest, and back of the red silk outfit worn by Qinghua when she flees from the tyrant. They no longer mark the flesh.
zh: 编舞借鉴了1950年代俄国芭蕾教师传入中国的古典芭蕾，也借鉴了中国戏曲。这种从两种资产阶级剧目中提取动作的合成，被用来倡扬无产阶级英雄。尤其是女舞者与过去脆弱、女性化的动作彻底决裂，贫苦劳动阶级被表现为坚强正面，而非粗俗。江青连补丁艺术这样的细节也亲自过问。无产阶级人物的破旧工作服不能因为“朴素写实”或马虎的补丁而显得平淡寒酸。江青指示剧团裁缝制作精美服装，在艺术上表现艰苦。在《红色娘子军》中（图5.04），清华逃离暴君时穿的红绸衣裤上，腿、臂、胸和背部画着长长的黑色鞭痕。它们不再标记肉体。

en: The company Commander notices the welts on her arms and asks her about herself. For generations Qinghua’s family suffered bloody oppression. Fury wells up in her heart. She pours out the story of the crimes of the Tyrant of the South.
(Solo dance.)
She pulls up her sleeves and reveals the whip marks covered with blood. (She does “ce shen xi tui,” “zhan chi dun zhuan” and “bei shen gui bu.”)

She tells of the tortures she endured in the Tyrant’s dungeon. (From “pang yue bu—jeté fermé” she turns to “zu jian bing li—soutenu en tournant.” In the “zao xing” she shows how she was chained in the Tyrant’s dungeon.) She tells how she was nearly beaten to death by the Tyrant in the coconut grove. (She does “tan hai fan she” and expresses her fury in “liang xiang.”)
Hong points out the cruelties inflicted on Qinghua’s family for generations as a lesson to the soldiers and peasants, saying:

“Her suffering is ours. Her hatred is ours. Slaves must arise. But only by taking up guns and waging revolution under the guidance of our great leader Chairman Mao and the Chinese Communist Party can we win a new world and liberate hundreds of millions of suffering people.” (He does “xi tui da tiao,” and “kong zhuan—tour en l’air” and performs “liang xiang” with an arm extended.)
zh: 连长发现她手臂上的鞭痕，询问她的身世。清华家世代遭受血腥压迫。怒火在她心中涌起。她倾诉南方恶霸的罪行。
（独舞。）
她挽起袖子，露出带血的鞭痕。
（她做“侧身吸腿”“展翅蹲转”“背身跪步”。）
她讲述在恶霸地牢中遭受的酷刑。（从“旁跃步——jeté fermé”转到“足尖并立——soutenu en tournant”。在“造型”中表现她被锁在恶霸地牢里。）
她讲述如何在椰林中被恶霸打得几乎死去。（她做“探海翻身”，在“亮相”中表达愤怒。）
洪常青指出清华一家世代遭受的苦难，以此教育战士和农民，说道：
“她的苦难就是我们的苦难。她的仇恨就是我们的仇恨。奴隶们要起来。但只有拿起枪，在伟大领袖毛主席和中国共产党的领导下进行革命，我们才能赢得新世界，解放数以亿计受苦的人民。”（他做“吸腿大跳”“空转——tour en l'air”，并伸臂“亮相”。）

en: On February 22, 1972, President Richard Nixon viewed a performance of
in Beijing. When he asked Jiang Qing to tell him the name of the director, she replied that it had been created by the masses. The follow day, the

ran a commentary on the ballet. The reviewer noted the accomplished achievement of ballet in China since it was first imported twenty years earlier when the Minister of Culture Mao Dun arranged for some of the best Bolshoi teachers to teach in Beijing. “Whatever the Chinese may feel toward the Russians nowadays, one debt of gratitude (two, if you include the atomic bomb) remains. It was the Russians who made it possible for the Chinese to combine toe slippers and rifles, and with splendid effect.”
The National Broadcasting Company aired a film version of the revolutionary model ballet on U.S. television on March 12, 1972.
zh: 1972年2月22日，理查德·尼克松总统在北京观看《红色娘子军》演出。当他请江青告诉他导演的名字时，她回答说这是群众创作的。第二天，《纽约时报》发表了一篇关于这部芭蕾的评论。评论者指出，自二十年前文化部长茅盾安排一些最好的莫斯科大剧院教师来京任教、芭蕾首次传入中国以来，中国取得了精湛成就。“无论中国人如今对俄国人是什么感情，仍欠着一笔感激（如果算上原子弹，就是两笔）。是俄国人使中国人能够把足尖鞋和步枪结合起来，而且效果极好。”
1972年3月12日，美国全国广播公司在美国电视上播放了这部革命样板芭蕾的电影版。

en: Qinghua steps out to take her bow in a new incarnation as international ambassador. Did Nixon grasp the symbolic importance of Hainan, an island nearly the size of Taiwan, which the Communists had liberated only in April 1950, after the Americans chose not to back the Nationalists in their claim to the territory? Amid Cold War tongue-in-cheek rhetoric about bombs and ballet slippers, Qinghua’s leap onto U.S. television screens signaled the future transfer of diplomatic recognition from Taipei to Beijing, under Jimmy Carter in 1979.
zh: 清华以国际大使的新化身走出来谢幕。尼克松是否领会了海南岛的象征意义？这个面积几乎与台湾相当的岛屿，直到1950年4月才被共产党解放，此前美国选择不支持国民党对该领土的主张。在关于炸弹和芭蕾鞋的冷战半开玩笑修辞中，清华跃上美国电视屏幕，预示着1979年吉米·卡特任内美国外交承认将从台北转向北京。

en: Progress
zh: 进步

en: A month after we first met, Li Tianpian and I chatted in her small room at the Central Minorities University. I’d gone that morning to her life drawing class to sketch together with her students. She had also set up an easel in the classroom to work on a study of the model. She lived in an older two-story dormitory in a forgotten corner of campus, behind a dusty cordoned-off site where workers were constructing a new classroom building. As we sat on her mattress on the floor, leaning our backs against the cool plaster wall, she told me about her youth.
zh: 我们第一次见面一个月后，李天翩和我在中央民族大学她的小房间里聊天。那天早晨我去了她的人体写生课，和她的学生一起画速写。她也在教室里支起画架，画一幅模特习作。她住在校园一个被遗忘角落的旧两层宿舍里；宿舍前是一片尘土飞扬、被围起来的工地，工人们正在那里建造新教学楼。我们坐在她铺在地板上的床垫上，背靠着冰凉的灰泥墙，她向我讲述自己的青年时代。

en: She grew up in the large northern industrial city of Shenyang in Liaoning Province. During the 1970s and 1980s, her father worked as a designer for a synthetic textile factory. It was a large light industry enterprise, like one of the many state-owned enterprises in the northeast region, each of which could employ up to tens of thousands of people. Her father designed advertisements, trade show materials, clothing, and brand logos. As early as the 1980s, when his work unit really prospered, he wore white dress shirts and flew on planes for business trips, especially to the south, where he served as a textile factory technical consultant. She remembered the gifts—rationed meat and fruit and piles of books—he brought back from his trips. And the benefits provided by the work unit were undeniably good.
zh: 她在北方工业大城辽宁沈阳长大。1970和1980年代，她父亲在一家合成纺织厂当设计师。那是大型轻工业企业，像东北地区许多国有企业一样，每家可能雇用数万人。她父亲设计广告、展会材料、服装和品牌标识。早在1980年代，他的单位真正繁荣时，他穿着白色衬衫，乘飞机出差，尤其是去南方，在那里担任纺织厂技术顾问。她记得他出差带回来的礼物——定量供应的肉和水果，还有成堆的书。工作单位提供的福利无可否认地好。

en: She liked drawing from a very young age. The kindergarten attached to the work unit had dedicated teachers who encouraged her to draw and paint, and she produced pictures—of Tiananmen Square, chickens, cars, and jeeps, she especially liked jeeps—to gain their praise. She attended a key elementary school, where the teachers entered her in all sorts of contests and exhibits. Her mother taught English at a middle school, and she asked one of the art teachers there to tutor Tianpian and her younger sister at his home, which he did for free. Comparing socialist ethics of communality with today’s market-driven social relations, Li Tianpian noted, “People were just like that back then. Today things are different. If I were to tutor you, we’d discuss how much for each class session, it’s very clear, one class, eighty, one hundred, whatever. Back then if a teacher saw you were a good kid, even if you weren’t in his class or school, just a friend’s child... well, he had a feeling of responsibility and would want to teach you. Teachers then were like that, they really didn’t think in terms of remuneration, but would just let you go to their house every day to paint.” This teacher eventually took her to the local government-run Young Pioneer Palace, which provided free art classes with expert teachers. She attended classes there every weekend with students of many different ages. During winter and summer vacations, they took trips out of the city to draw from life. Her mother spent all of her money so that Tianpian could take trips to places like Mount Tai. She entered more contests and exhibits and started winning prizes. She laughed, “I had a big pile of awards.... I was really proud of myself, thought I was really something.”
zh: 她从小就喜欢画画。单位附属幼儿园里尽心尽责的老师鼓励她画画，她画天安门广场、鸡、汽车和吉普车——她特别喜欢吉普车——来赢得表扬。她上了重点小学，老师让她参加各种比赛和展览。她母亲在一所中学教英语，请那里的一位美术老师辅导天翩和妹妹；老师在自己家里免费教她们。李天翩比较社会主义的共同体伦理与今天市场驱动的社会关系时说：“那时的人就是这样。现在不同了。如果我给你辅导，我们会商量每节课多少钱，很清楚，一节课八十、一百，随便。那时，老师要是看出你是个好孩子，即使你不是他班上的、不是他学校的，只是朋友的孩子……他就有一种责任感，想教你。那时的老师就是这样，真的不考虑报酬，就是让你每天去他家画画。”这位老师最终把她带到当地政府办的少年宫，那里有专家教师免费上美术课。她每个周末和许多不同年龄的学生一起上课。寒暑假，他们出城写生。母亲花光所有钱，让天翩去泰山等地旅行。她参加更多比赛和展览，开始获奖。她笑着说：“我有一大堆奖……我特别自豪，觉得自己真了不起。”

en: She tested effortlessly into a key middle school and also started attending after-school classes at the Lu Xun Academy of Fine Arts, located near her home in Shenyang. These classes offered university entrance exam coaching for students who wanted to test into art academies. At twelve years old, she was one of the youngest students, and she watched as the older students—some from technical or art schools—tried to pass the fiercely competitive entrance exam. Many tried year after year without passing before they finally gave up. Some did very well on the art section, but couldn’t get high enough scores on the general humanities exam. In her second year of middle school, she met a girl who had tested into the attached high school of the Central Academy in Beijing and gave her the idea to register for the exam the following year. She passed it easily.
zh: 她轻松考进一所重点中学，也开始在沈阳家附近的鲁迅美术学院上课后班。这些班为想考美术学院的学生提供高考辅导。十二岁时，她是最年轻的学生之一，看着年纪更大的学生——有些来自中专或美术学校——努力通过竞争激烈的入学考试。许多人年复一年考不上，最终放弃。有些人的美术部分考得很好，却无法在文化课考试中取得足够高的分数。中学二年级时，她遇到一个考进北京中央美术学院附中的女孩，萌生了下一年报考的念头。她轻松通过。

en: In 1985, she moved to Beijing, where she spent three years at the high school run by the Central Academy of Fine Arts. When she first arrived, the behavior and dress of some of the older students shocked her. In contrast with the neat school uniform she’d grown up wearing, they dressed casually in the latest city fashions. They danced disco, listened to Michael Jackson and Madonna, and had multiple boyfriends. Gradually she adapted to life at the school, where most of them also lived, but about certain things, especially romance and sex, she felt she had a deep-rooted traditionalism. Their schedule was divided into half days of regular subjects and half days of art classes. In the beginning, she really liked sculpture, but eventually decided to specialize in oil painting. It was one of the most difficult courses to test into at an art academy. In her third year, she registered for the university exam, and again easily tested into the China Academy of Art in Hangzhou.
zh: 1985年，她搬到北京，在中央美术学院附属高中读了三年。刚到时，一些年长学生的行为和穿着让她震惊。与她从小穿的整洁校服形成对比，他们穿着随意，追逐最新城市时尚。他们跳迪斯科，听迈克尔·杰克逊和麦当娜，同时交好几个男朋友。她逐渐适应了这所大部分人也住校的学校生活，但在某些事情上，尤其是爱情和性，她觉得自己有一种根深蒂固的传统主义。课程安排是半天普通科目、半天美术课。起初她很喜欢雕塑，最终决定专攻油画。那是美术学院最难考进的课程之一。第三年，她报名高考，再次轻松考进杭州的中国美术学院。

en: She entered the academy in the fall of 1988 as the youngest of thirteen students in the first-year oil painting class. New ideas, trends, and exhibits had begun to explode onto the art scene; suddenly everyone seemed to have their own styles. She recalled that she and her classmates spent all of their time enthusiastically reading, thinking, discussing. When the student movement in the spring of 1989 began gaining nationwide momentum, she joined other students in the streets. But she was young; she said she didn’t really understand the political situation and just went along like a child going to see the excitement, like an observer of a theatrical production. Classes had come to a standstill. Her parents urged her not to participate in the protests. After June 4, when the central government shut down communication and transportation lines between north and south, she grew frightened. She thought if regular travel weren’t resumed, she wouldn’t be able to see her family. If a war broke out, her life would be ruined.
zh: 1988年秋，她入学，成为油画系一年级十三名学生中最年轻的一个。新观念、新潮流、新展览开始爆发于艺术界；突然每个人似乎都有自己的风格。她回忆说自己和同学把所有时间都热情地用于阅读、思考、讨论。1989年春学生运动在全国获得势头时，她和其他学生一起走上街头。但她还年轻；她说自己并不真正理解政治局势，只是像孩子看热闹一样随大流，像戏剧演出的旁观者。课程停摆。父母劝她不要参加抗议。六四之后，中央政府切断南北通讯和交通，她害怕起来。她想，如果正常交通不恢复，她就见不到家人；如果爆发战争，她的人生就毁了。

en: “Let’s not talk about this anymore,” she told me. “My life in university was really ideal.” She graduated after four years, one of the eight students left in their original class of thirteen and one of only two women. A few had dropped out. Two had gone to Russia. She moved back to Shenyang where she had been assigned to the city’s Cultural Center (

). She didn’t like this unstructured lifestyle; she felt aimless, with no pressure or inspiration. She received assignments to teach master classes at various places around the city. She painted on her own, but soon she decided she wanted to continue her studies. A national rule stipulated that after two years of work, one could apply to graduate school. But after two years the director of the Cultural Center refused to give her permission. Whatever he said stood, and she felt confused and paralyzed. She panicked, thinking she would spend her life buried in a place surrounded by people who came to work to read the newspaper and drink tea. She took on some work at an advertising agency, but this lifestyle did not appeal to her either. Her bosses and customers treated her like a girl rather than a talented designer. They expected her to stay out late at night to accompany them at banquets. She described her repulsion at having to greet new clients who held onto her hand for too long. She quit. After four years at the Cultural Center, the director retired, and she immediately registered for the graduate school exam. Again, she passed all of the hurdles smoothly and returned to Hangzhou.
zh: “我们别谈这个了，”她对我说，“我的大学时光真的很理想。”四年后她毕业，原来十三人的班上只剩八人，她是仅有的两名女生之一。几人退学，两人去了俄罗斯。她回到沈阳，被分配到市文化馆。她不喜欢这种没有结构的生活方式；她觉得没有目标，没有压力，也没有灵感。她接受安排，到城里各处教授大师班。她自己画画，但很快决定想要继续深造。国家规定，工作两年后才能报考研究生。但两年后，文化馆馆长拒绝放她走。他说了算，她感到困惑，束手无策。她惊恐地想到，自己会一辈子埋没在这个地方，周围都是上班看报喝茶的人。她在一家广告公司找了点活，但这种生活也不吸引她。老板和客户把她当小姑娘，而不是有才华的设计师。他们希望她熬夜陪宴。她描述自己不得不迎接新客户、对方久久拉着她的手时的厌恶。她辞职了。在文化馆工作四年后，馆长退休，她立刻报考研究生。她再次顺利通过所有关卡，回到杭州。

en: Since receiving her master’s degree and moving to Beijing to teach at the Central Minorities University, she tried, unsuccessfully in her own opinion, to leave behind the classical, realist style that enabled her to test into progressively advanced levels of the official art education system. But she also struggled with a sense that oil painting didn’t really matter in the new economy. She reflected on a spiritual reversal, in which material practicality now mattered more than anything else, with those in the arts privileging design. She lamented, “In the past some poets really gained people’s worship, poets, writers, painters. But not anymore. Now they worship people who are financially successful, who have high social and economic standing.... Sometimes I think about what my function in society is. For example, I have continued to teach students, to teach them to follow the road I’ve taken. When I educate them, when I guide them, it’s not with the same lofty ideals I used to have. I can no longer tell them that to be a painter, to be an artist, to devote oneself to art is really worth pursuing.” Laughing with resignation, she concluded, “I used to think I was more accomplished than other people, I wanted to take the hardest tests and go to the best schools. But suddenly I realized that society had stealthily changed. I already wasn’t so remarkable. I’d become that kind of person on the margins of society, a painter.”
zh: 获得硕士学位、搬到北京在中央民族大学任教后，她试图摆脱那种使她逐级考进官方美术教育体系的古典写实风格，但按她自己的说法，没有成功。她也挣扎于一种感觉：油画在新经济中并不真正重要。她反思一种精神反转：物质实用如今比什么都重要，艺术界人士则推崇设计。她哀叹：“过去有些诗人真的受到人们崇拜，诗人、作家、画家。现在不再如此。现在他们崇拜经济成功、社会和经济地位高的人……有时我会想我在社会中的功能是什么。比如，我一直在教学生，教他们走我走过的路。当我教育他们、引导他们时，已经不再带着过去那种崇高理想。我再也不能告诉他们，当画家、当艺术家、献身艺术真正值得追求。”她无奈地笑着总结：“我曾觉得自己比别人有成就，想考最难的试，上最好的学校。但突然意识到，社会已经悄悄改变。我已经不那么出众。我成了那种处在社会边缘的人——一个画家。”

en: A parallel runs between the way she narrated her life as an art student and teacher and how she reflected on the life course of her parents. She described the feeling of success and accomplishment her father had when his factory reached the height of its production. Eventually his position (ironically, he

a designer, but for a state-run company) fell victim to the privatization drive of the 1990s. She told the denouement of their story, “But now, the national enterprises have all gone under, everyone is laid off, and his heart often cannot bear it. In fact, when things first started to turn bad, he got sick for a while. He can’t accept this reality psychologically. The two of them, my father and mother’s generation, night and day, they offered up their lives. Sometimes I really think about it, I don’t want to do the same.”
zh: 她讲述自己作为艺术学生和教师的经历，与她反思父母的人生轨迹之间存在平行。她描述父亲在工厂生产达到顶峰时的成功感和成就感。最终，他的职位（讽刺的是，他是一名设计师，但在一家国营公司）成为1990年代私有化浪潮的牺牲品。她讲述他们故事的结局：“但现在，国有企业都垮了，大家都下岗，他心里常常承受不了。其实，事情刚开始变坏时，他病了一阵。他在心理上无法接受这个现实。他们那一代，我父亲和母亲，日日夜夜奉献了一生。有时我真的想到这些，就不想重蹈覆辙。”

en: In an attempt to find a way out of her current situation, she frequently turned to the topic of marriage. She longed to leave behind her cramped teacher’s dorm room, without its own kitchen or bathroom, where painted canvases rested against bookshelves and bars covered the sole window. At thirty-one, she felt like she was getting too old to stay single. Three of her friends from school all got married around the same time a few years ago. She really envied them at the time, but now all of them are divorced. One of them had a husband who drank and gambled and beat her, but they got to the United States before she divorced him. The husband of another often left home for long business trips, and they gradually grew apart. The third left her husband for one of his friends who helped her apply to study abroad in England. If she got married, she would have better housing, but she still harbored the ideal of finding someone she would want to stay with for life.
zh: 为了摆脱当前处境，她经常转向婚姻话题。她渴望离开那间没有独立厨房和卫生间、画布靠书架立着、唯一窗户装有铁栏的狭小教师宿舍。三十一岁的她觉得自己单身太久。学生时代的三个朋友几年前几乎同时结婚。当时她真羡慕她们，但现在都离婚了。其中一个的丈夫酗酒、赌博还打她，但她在离婚前已经到了美国。另一个的丈夫经常长期出差，两人渐渐疏远。第三个离开丈夫，投向丈夫一个朋友的怀抱，后者帮她申请去英国留学。如果结婚，她会有更好的住房，但她仍怀有找到一个愿与之共度一生的人的理想。

en: Her other option for attaining a more comfortable life was learning to paint the kinds of paintings that sell well. She had sold a few paintings, studio still life and figure paintings, through a Taiwanese gallery. She planned to look around galleries more to try to understand what did well on the market. She claimed that she had grown up and realized the significant difference between men and women. She felt she didn’t have enough physical strength to do the work required, to do enough research, to paint large paintings without wearing herself out. Even though she used to be able to do all these things without a problem, she convinced herself now that it was men’s work.
zh: 获得更舒适生活的另一个选择，是学会画畅销的画。她通过一家台湾画廊卖过几幅画，画室静物和人物。她打算多逛画廊，了解市场上什么卖得好。她声称自己长大了，意识到男女之间的重大差异。她觉得自己没有足够的体力完成所需工作，做足够的研究，画大画而不把自己累垮。尽管她过去做所有这些都毫无问题，她现在却让自己相信那是男人的工作。

en: Calculation
zh: 盘算

en: We sat again on Li Tianpian’s mattress on the floor toward the end of that summer. The lights were turned off to keep the room cooler. Sweat beaded our faces as we ate popsicles and watched a line of ants crawling up the wall. She told me it wasn’t worth trying to stop their invasion. I asked about the man she was dating when I last saw her. She looked a little annoyed and told me she no longer seemed able to attract him. When she called him, he didn’t answer. When he finally returned her call a few days later, he gave a vague excuse. She sighed and said he didn’t seem serious about her. He only wanted to hang out in her room, talking or holding her. She thought they should go out sometimes. It was weird that he only wanted to come to her room, like he didn’t want to be seen in public together.
zh: 那个夏天快结束时，我们又坐在李天翩铺在地板上的床垫上。为了凉快，灯关着。我们吃着冰棍，看一队蚂蚁爬上墙，汗珠挂在脸上。她告诉我，阻止它们入侵不值得。我问起上次见面时她正在交往的那个男人。她显得有点恼火，说她似乎再也吸引不了他。她打电话他不接。几天后他终于回电话，给了一个含糊的借口。她叹口气，说他对她不认真。他只想待在她房间里聊天或抱她。她觉得他们有时应该出去。他只想来她房间，这很奇怪，好像不愿被人看见他们在一起。

en: She felt self-conscious. Most people thought she should be married at her age, but she didn’t want to get married just for better housing. If she remained single and a teacher at the university, her quality of life would not improve significantly. She said she didn’t want much, just an apartment big enough for her parents to come stay with her and enjoy life in Beijing when they wanted. “Are Americans like this,” she asked me, “do they think about repaying their parents later in life? I don’t want much.”
zh: 她感到不自在。大多数人认为她这个年纪应该结婚，但她不想仅为改善住房而结婚。如果保持单身，继续当大学教师，她的生活质量不会显著改善。她说自己要求不多，只想有一套足够大的公寓，让父母想来时能和她住在一起，享受北京生活。“美国人会这样吗？”她问我，“他们会在以后的人生里想着报答父母吗？我的要求不多。”

en: She had asked me to come over that day because she wanted to talk about what it would take to study in the United States. We discussed the need for her to improve her English skills. She had been accepted for a two-month artist residency at the well-known Vermont Studio Center, where she had also been given a fellowship to cover studio and living expenses. I translated the information they sent her and helped her fill out various forms. She asked what museums she should go to see in New York if her visa for the trip came through. A few of her classmates now lived in New York, where they got by painting portraits for hire. They’d told her that in a good month, they could make two to three thousand dollars. I watched her calculate the figures in her head. She concluded that if she scrimped and could save a thousand dollars a month, she would have to work for three years like this to accumulate enough for an apartment in Beijing.
zh: 那天她请我来，是想谈谈去美国学习需要什么。我们讨论了她需要提高英语。她已被著名的佛蒙特工作室中心（Vermont Studio Center）为期两个月的艺术家驻留项目录取，并获得覆盖画室和生活费用的奖学金。我翻译了对方寄给她的材料，帮她填写各种表格。她问如果旅行签证获准，到纽约应该去看哪些博物馆。她的几个同学现在住在纽约，靠画肖像为生。他们告诉她，行情好的月份能挣两三千美元。我看她在心里算账。她得出结论，如果省吃俭用，每月存一千美元，就得这样工作三年，才能攒够在北京买一套公寓的钱。

en: Postcard
zh: 明信片

en: Although I kept the postcard of Li Tianpian’s painting

taped to the wall over my desk, I was never able to see the four large canvases of the original work. With no space to keep it in her room, she had stored it away in a school warehouse. Reduced from its monumental size to an easily circulated postcard, the women it depicted might be privately viewed and easily forgotten. However, over the months I gradually got to know Li Tianpian better, its layered imagery stuck in my mind. It contained within its frame a history of Chinese art academy oil painting, discontinuities between reality and representation, and Li Tianpian’s place in a national history signified and resignified through practices of visualizing women’s bodies. How could the Red Detachment women have married the enemy? How laughable, this revolutionary romance thrown off like an old set of clothes. How could she now feel that, as a woman, she didn’t have enough physical strength to paint large paintings without wearing herself out, and yet consider painting foreigners’ portraits for three years?
zh: 虽然我把李天翩《红色纪念品》的明信片一直贴在我书桌上方的墙上，却始终没能看到原作的四块大画布。她房间里没有存放空间，只好把画存到学校仓库。从纪念碑式的尺寸缩减为便于流通的明信片，画中女性可能被私下观看，也容易被遗忘。然而，随着几个月过去，我逐渐更了解李天翩，它层叠的意象始终留在我脑海里。它的画框内包含中国学院油画史、现实与再现之间的断裂，以及李天翩在一部通过女性身体视觉化实践而被意指和重新意指的民族历史中的位置。红色娘子军的女人们怎么可能嫁给敌人？多么可笑，这种革命浪漫主义像一套旧衣服一样被抛掉。她如今怎么会觉得自己作为女人没有足够体力画大画而不累垮，却又考虑画三年外国人肖像？

en: Ghosts
zh: 幽灵

en: I had just emerged from the subway at the end of October 2001 when I got a call from Li Tianpian on my cell phone. Amid the noise of the street, I heard her bright laughter on the other end as she asked me if I knew that it was the American holiday Halloween. She invited me to go to a disco with her that night. Some of her friends who went to the Halloween party the previous year had a great time. They dressed up in crazy outfits and danced with all of the foreigners there.
zh: 2001年10月底，我刚从地铁出来，手机就响起李天翩的来电。在街道的噪音中，我听到电话那头她爽朗的笑声，她问我知不知道当天是美国的万圣节。她邀请我当晚和她一起去迪斯科。她的一些朋友去年参加万圣节派对，玩得很开心。他们穿着疯狂服装，和那里所有外国人跳舞。

en: I begged off saying I’d been feeling tired lately. Since our last meeting, I’d gone back to the United States for a short trip. I suggested we get together soon because I had something I wanted to give her. I’d brought back a small present for her, a map of art museums in New York. She said something about still not having enough money for her plane ticket, but we’d talk more soon. I promised to call, and then we hung up.
zh: 我推说最近很累。自上次见面后，我回美国短期旅行。我建议很快见面，因为我有东西要送她。我给她带回一件小礼物，一张纽约艺术博物馆地图。她说了些机票钱还不够之类的话，但我们很快再聊。我答应打电话，然后挂了。

en: Her Halloween phone call reminded me of the funny story she told me about first arriving in Beijing from Shenyang to attend high school. The class above hers had organized a welcome party. They held it at night in one of the classrooms. They put on music and started doing what she called “disco dance.” Then they turned the lights off and continued dancing. She stood there in her old school uniform thinking, “What are they doing?” When she got back to her room, she wrote in her diary that these students were a “host of demons dancing wildly.”
zh: 她的万圣节来电让我想起她讲过的一个有趣故事：她刚从沈阳到北京上高中时，高一级的班级组织了一场欢迎会。晚会晚上在一间教室举行。他们放音乐，开始跳她所说的“迪斯科”。然后他们关掉灯，继续跳。她穿着旧校服站在那里想：“他们在干什么？”回到宿舍后，她在日记里写道，这些学生是“群魔乱舞”。

en: I called her several times that winter and spring, whenever I noticed the plastic-coated Artwise Manhattan map on my bookshelf, but no one ever answered.
zh: 那年冬天和次年春天，每当我看到书架上那张塑封的 Artwise 曼哈顿地图，就给她打电话，但始终无人接听。

en: Gone
zh: 离去

en: Several months later, just over a year since I’d first met Li Tianpian, I bumped into Yuan Yaomin at an exhibit opening. She asked if I’d heard. I shook my head, not understanding the question. She pulled me aside and said, “She’s gone.”
zh: 几个月后，距我第一次见到李天翩刚过一年，我在一个展览开幕式上遇到袁耀敏。她问我听说了没有。我摇摇头，不明白她在问什么。她把我拉到一边说：“她走了。”

en: Li Tianpian had successfully gotten a visa to the United States, but hadn’t been able to get together the money for a plane ticket. She managed to reschedule her residency at the Vermont Studio Center for a later time. In late November, she went out with a male friend. She was worried about still being unmarried in her thirties, and many friends had started setting up dates for her. Her date was driving. They left Beijing for the nearby countryside to take photos. There was an accident. They both died in the crash on November 24. Yuan Yaomin whispered to me that this was the date of her original visa for the United States.
zh: 李天翩成功拿到美国签证，却凑不齐机票钱。她设法把佛蒙特工作室中心的驻留推迟到更晚。11月下旬，她和一位男性朋友外出。她担心自己三十多岁仍未婚，许多朋友开始给她安排相亲。她的相亲对象开车。他们离开北京去附近乡下拍照。发生了车祸。两人都在11月24日的撞车中丧生。袁耀敏低声对我说，那正是她原定赴美签证的日期。

en: After I heard this news, I walked around in a daze for an hour or more. The gallery I’d gone to for the exhibition stood in section of Beijing that, like many others, was in the middle of being razed. I walked along the ruins of what had once been the southern edge of the old city wall. I could already see more of the ruined wall than a few months before. The ramshackle one-story dwellings that had once butted up three deep against the wall had been reduced to piles of bricks, garbage, and dry dirt. When I had walked along this stretch of road a year or half a year earlier, I’d watched people hanging their clothes out to dry on wire lines strung between trees and noticed the even spacing of the bricks weighing down tar paper on the roofs. The remaining rubble now struck me as one of the city’s many open wounds, an injury made temporarily manifest, that would soon be covered up with shiny glass and chrome, like the high-rise office and shopping complexes across the street.
zh: 听到这个消息后，我恍惚地走了一个多小时。我去看展览的那家画廊位于北京一个像许多其他地方一样正在被夷平的区域。我沿着旧城墙南缘的废墟走，那城墙曾经矗立。我已经能看到比几个月前更多的残墙。曾经紧贴城墙、纵深三排的破旧平房，已经化为砖堆、垃圾和干土。一年或半年前，我走在这段路上时，看见人们把衣服晾在树间拉起的铁丝上，注意到压住屋顶油毡纸的砖块间距均匀。如今剩下的瓦砾让我觉得是这座城市许多敞开的伤口之一，一种暂时显现的损伤，很快就会被闪亮的玻璃和铬合金覆盖，就像街对面高层办公和商业综合体那样。

en: My mind turned to a traffic accident I had recently witnessed near my apartment. A woman lay on the inclined side of an exit ramp from the second ring road, with a crumpled bicycle next to her. She lay on her back, with the glasses on her face bumped at an awkward angle. Vomit ran from her half-open mouth across her cheek and onto her chest. The police had begun drawing a white line around her body.
zh: 我的思绪转向最近在我公寓附近目睹的一场交通事故。一个女人躺在二环路出口匝道的斜坡上，旁边是一辆压扁的自行车。她仰面躺着，脸上的眼镜歪成别扭的角度。呕吐物从她半张的嘴里流过脸颊，落到胸口。警察已经开始在她身体周围画白线。

en: It was hot and dusty. The sky was heavy with clouds and pollution. It wouldn’t start raining for several more hours. All I had were my rambling questions on tape and her cheerful voice trying to respond to my inquiry into her career as an artist.
zh: 天气炎热，尘土飞扬。天空被乌云和污染压得很重。还要过几个小时才会下雨。我只有磁带上那些漫无边际的问题，以及她快乐的声音，试图回应我对她艺术生涯的询问。

en: Remains
zh: 遗存

en: When I first explained my research to Li Tianpian, she told me my study would possess objectivity; I would recognize things that she could not. All I have are small fragments, symbols of outdated, bankrupt glory and idealism, and her hopeful laughter. The latter, her story, resists the social scientist’s task of analysis. I want only to do justice, to memorialize in a tableau vivant of costumed figures, each in the drag of its own era, the failed heroics of history, which layered together may communicate something about what gets suppressed at the moment of representation. What remains unrepresentable in heroic figuration.
zh: 第一次向李天翩解释我的研究时，她告诉我，我的研究会有客观性；我会认出她认不出的东西。我所有的只是一些小碎片，过时、破产的荣耀与理想主义的象征，以及她满怀希望的笑声。后者，她的故事，抗拒社会科学家分析的任务。我只想做到公正，用一组身着各自时代装扮的人物活人画来纪念历史上失败的英雄主义；层叠在一起，它们或许能传达在再现时刻被压抑的东西。英雄形象中无法再现的东西。

en: Picking her way through a ruined landscape of representation, Li Tianpian painted the Red Detachment in the wake of their rise and fall, recuperating their image even though it must be read through everything that has happened since: the political excesses of the Cultural Revolution; China’s bid to “link tracks” not with world socialism but transnational capitalism; the transformation of the state art system that trained her; and the emergence of a postsocialist allegory about how socialism repressed “natural” gender with its androgynous representations. Meanwhile, Li Tianpian struggled with the revaluation of art in China according to an international market, in which her representational skills had become marginal. She calculated how she might get by in a rapidly changing society: by either attracting an entrepreneur as a marriage partner or learning to paint the kinds of paintings that would sell well. She was bothered not necessarily by how art misrepresents, but by how mundane reality is when you slip behind the scenes of the typical and end up marrying the enemy.
zh: 李天翩在再现的废墟景观中择路而行，在红色娘子军起落之后描绘她们，修复她们的形象，尽管这形象必须通过此后发生的一切来解读：文化大革命的政治过激行为；中国寻求“接轨”的对象不是世界社会主义，而是跨国资本主义；培养她的国家艺术体制转型；以及一种后社会主义寓言的出现——社会主义如何以其中性化的形象再现压抑“自然”性别。与此同时，李天翩挣扎于按国际市场对中国艺术重新估价，她赖以生存的再现技能在其中已被边缘化。她盘算如何在一个迅速变化的社会中生存：要么吸引一位企业家作为婚姻伴侣，要么学会画畅销的画。困扰她的未必是艺术如何错误再现，而是当你溜到典型的幕后、最终嫁给敌人时，平凡现实是何等模样。

en: The narrow addition of her self-portrait, dividing a space between those red women of the past, salvages them from a fate of becoming discardable national kitsch, the kind especially enjoyed by foreign tourists, and turns their twentieth-century pageant into a play of sorrow rather than nostalgia. Her presence within turns the image into something doubled-edged: an intensified collection of ideals passionately pursued, a repository of utopian dream, inevitably flattened into heart-breaking two-dimensionality. The cult of individual authorship steps out in the guise of privatization and market economics. Her style slides sideways out of time. The superstructure again appears to lag behind the base. Naturalized gender competes with class as a meaningful social category. Art and marriage alike shimmer like commodities and promise access to the world.
zh: 她自画像的窄小增补，在过去那些红色女性之间分出一片空间，把她们从沦为可丢弃的民族媚俗品——外国游客尤其喜欢的那种——的命运中抢救出来，把她们二十世纪的华彩演出变成一出悲伤而非怀旧的戏剧。她的在场使图像变得双刃：一份被热情追求的理想的强化集合，一个乌托邦梦想的仓库，不可避免地压扁为令人心碎的二维。个人作者身份的崇拜以私有化和市场经济的伪装登场。她的风格侧滑出时间。上层建筑再次显得落后于基础。自然化的性别与阶级竞争作为有意义的社会范畴。艺术和婚姻都像商品一样闪光，许诺通往世界。

en: For many months after I learned of Li Tianpian’s death, I couldn’t listen to our taped conversations, let alone contemplate constraining her life with my interpretation. But her painting, once stored in a school warehouse, disappeared. Reduced from its monumental size to a fading postcard, the women it depicted stood little chance of being remembered. So I began to write in order to not forget. For the sake of the women buried in oblivion, whose bodies have been overwritten by male and national desire, I want to remember.
zh: 得知李天翩去世后的好几个月里，我无法听我们的谈话录音，更不用说用我的解释去约束她的人生。但她的画作，曾存放在学校仓库，消失了。从纪念碑式的尺寸缩减为一张褪色的明信片，画中女性几乎没有被记住的可能。所以我开始写作，为了不忘记。为了那些被湮没的女性，那些身体被男性和国家欲望覆盖的女性，我要记住。

en: remains full of mytho-historical symbols frozen in time. It teems with images of unrealized potential. It will not be recognized in the current climate as a great or even a good painting, but this is exactly what infuses it with historical meaning. It is a shuang nü ti over time, a double-figured dialectic of women attempting escape who force us to question the relationship between the representation and the real.
zh: 《红色纪念品》仍然充满凝固于时间中的神话历史符号。它满是未实现潜能的形象。在当前风气中，它不会被承认为一幅伟大的画，甚至算不上一幅好画，但这恰恰赋予它历史意义。它是一幅跨越时间的双女体，一种试图逃离的女性双重形象辩证法，迫使我们质疑再现与现实的关系。
